title: What a butler is actually for
subtitle: Not pouring. Fixing — with the standing to move a dinner without you queueing for it.

text: He is not a waiter with a better title. He is a fixer with standing.
sub: The value is not service delivered to you in the suite. It is friction removed elsewhere on the ship, before you ever knew it existed.

items.head: Moving a booking
items.body: A table changed, a treatment shifted, a tour swapped — without you standing at a desk at four o'clock.

items.head: Timing around the port
items.body: Breakfast on the terrace at half six because the tender at Katakolon goes early. Ask the night before.

items.head: Pressing and packing
items.body: Everything ready before the captain's evening, and again on the last night when nobody wants to fold anything.

items.head: Knowing who to ring
items.body: Which shore agent, which restaurant ashore, which member of crew can actually solve your problem.

quote: Tell him how you take your coffee, when you like to eat, and what you never want offered. The week arranges itself after that.

text: Brief him on the first afternoon. Ten minutes, once.
sub: Preferences, timings, and what you'd rather never be offered. Done properly it's the only such conversation you need — everything after that happens without discussion.

title: What would you actually ask a butler for?
body: Tell me in the comments. The good answers are always duller and more useful than the brochure ones.
